title: 3946. Maximum Number of Items From Sale I

examples.explanation: You can buy 2 copies of item 0 and 1 copy of item 2 for a total cost of 2 * 2 + 4 = 8, which is not greater than budget = 9. Buying item 2 gives 1 free copy of item 0, because factor2 = 3 divides factor0 = 6. You leave with 3 purchased copies and 1 free copy, for a total of 4 item copies.

You can buy 1 copy of item 0, 1 copy of item 1, and 2 copies of item 2 for a total cost of 4 + 2 + 2 * 1 = 8. Buying item 0 gives 1 free copy of items 2, 3, and 4. Buying item 1 gives 1 free copy of items 3 and 4. Buying item 2 gives 1 free copy of item 4. Thus, you receive 6 free copies. You leave with 4 purchased copies and 6 free copies, for a total of 10 item copies.

hints: Precompute for every possible factor f, how many items have a factor divisible by f.
Buying the first copy of item i is special: it gives the purchased copy plus one free copy of every other item whose factor is divisible by factor_i.
Buying more copies of the same item does not create more free copies, so after the first copy, each extra purchase only adds one item copy.

This suggests a knapsack-style DP over item types and remaining budget, where each item can either be skipped, bought for the first time, or bought additional times after it has already been activated.
